prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1147; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness, onset within hours of the incident. Liability appears clear based on initial statements and photos from the scene. Claimant is unrepresented at this time. Advised of the claims process and asked to provide medical records and treatment details as they become available.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes ongoing whiplash symptoms, including headaches and reduced range of motion when turning the head. Claimant states they visited an urgent care clinic the day after the collision and was given a neck brace and pain medication. Requested copies of all discharge paperwork and the name of the treating provider. Reminded claimant they may consult an attorney at any time and that this adjuster cannot provide legal advice.

Entry 3: Received police report from the responding agency. Report confirms the third-party driver was cited for following too closely. No witness statements listed. Vehicle damage estimates reviewed: rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly on the claimant's vehicle. Repair estimate requested from the approved body shop. Photos on file match the reported damage pattern.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the urgent care clinic. Diagnosis recorded as cervical strain consistent with whiplash-type injury. Follow-up visit with a primary care physician scheduled per the discharge notes. Claimant has not yet submitted physical therapy referral paperwork. Called claimant to confirm whether the follow-up appointment has occurred and requested updated treatment information.

Entry 5: Claimant reports continued neck discomfort but says they are returning to work with some modified duties. Reviewed the file for completeness: police report, photos, repair estimate, and initial medical records are on file. Outstanding items include the primary care notes and any physical therapy records. Set a diary reminder to follow up with claimant and the treating provider. No settlement discussions have taken place at this stage.
